cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, a family of Levites (2 Chronicles 20:19), and they skip the warm-up completely: "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain." No small talk, friend, straight to the praise.

Then they start bragging on that mountain: Mount Zion is beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon. They talk about it the way I talk about a tray of cookies fresh out of the oven, and friend, I do NOT stop talking.

cards.question: The song gives Mount Zion one more title. Whose city does it call Zion?

cards.text: Zion's got citadels. And the song tells you exactly who's in them.

cards.question: The song says God is in Zion's citadels and has shown Himself to be a fortress.

cards.text: Then this: "For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together." Not one king, friend, a whole CROWD of kings, and I'd be checking every lock on the bakery door.

cards.question: The kings get close enough to see God's city. They are astounded, and they ___ in terror.

cards.text: Trembling seizes them right there, anguish like a woman in labor. I know that tremble, friend: every time the junk drawer opened, I shook just like that, and all anybody wanted was the scissors.

cards.question: Then the song speaks right to God about the ships of Tarshish. What does it say God wrecked them with?

cards.text: Now the people talk about the city of the LORD of Hosts. They'd heard all about it, and they've got an update.

cards.question: The people had heard about the city of the LORD of Hosts. What do they say about it now?

answers.text: They have seen it for themselves
It was only an old story
They are still waiting to see it

cards.question: After the kings flee from God's city, the people say God will establish her forever.

cards.text: Kings ran, ships sank, and now the song gets quiet and goes within God's temple. The people slow down there and think about one thing.

cards.question: Within God's temple, what do the people contemplate?
The song tells God that His name reaches only as far as Zion's walls.

cards.text: His name goes to the ends of the earth, and the song says His right hand is full of righteousness. Then Mount Zion is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice right along with it.

cards.question: Mount Zion is glad and the daughters of Judah rejoice on account of God's ___.

cards.text: Then the song gives an order: "March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers," then consider her ramparts and tour her citadels. This psalm wants you to get your steps in, friend, and I'm HOPPING that whole lap, gold base and all.

cards.question: The song says to walk around Zion counting towers and touring citadels so you can tell the next generation.

cards.text: Then the last line: "For this God is our God forever and ever;" Friend, I got swapped out once for a shinier stamper, so trust me, FOREVER and ever is the best news in this whole song.

cards.question: The song's last line says this God will be their guide. For how long?
